ops.text: Repeated requantization is the regime described by the bit-growth law of Veldhuis et al. (2026), in which the bits needed per state entry rise by about 0.62 for every doubling of the context; a single rounding per stored checkpoint does not compound in this way.

new_bib.text: J. Veldhuis, F. Postma, R. Zwart, and M. Dekkers (2026). How many bits does a recurrent state need? Context-length scaling of state precision in Mamba and gated linear attention. arXiv preprint.
